mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.3% triggers a preemptive equity risk premium as investors anticipate future rate hikes, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3% in the current month
failure_condition: Over the next 20 days, SPX 20d forward returns are not statistically different from zero (t-test p > 0.05) during confirmed inflation spikes above 0.3%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in PAYEMS labor cost growth above 0.5% signals wage pressures that prompt equity market participants to anticipate higher corporate profits, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS grows > 0.5% month-over-month for three consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20d forward returns over the 60-day horizon are negative or flat during the identified wage acceleration period (rolling mean p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in RSAFS industrial production exceeding 2% indicates weakening supply-side demand, which elevates uncertainty and elevates equity risk premia, yielding negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS declines > 2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: During confirmed supply contraction, SPX 5d forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in INDPRO (≥ 3% month-over-month) coinciding with a rise in HOUST housing starts (< -2% MoM) signals a dual supply shock, compressing equity valuations and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month AND HOUST < previous month, with INDPRO drop ≥ 3% and HOUST decline ≥ 2%
failure_condition: SPX 20d forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the identified dual contraction episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in FEDFUNDS below 2% for three consecutive months, absent other inflationary pressures, creates a risk-off environment where the S&P 500 anticipates lower growth and produces negative 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2% for three consecutive months and CPIAUCSL < 0.2% over the same period
failure_condition: SPX 20d forward returns over the 60-day window are not negative in at least 70% of such episodes (rolling quantile).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in UNRATE above 4% in a single month signals labor market tightening, prompting equity market participants to price in wage growth and higher earnings, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 4% in the current month
failure_condition: SPX 20d forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during the identified tightening episode.

mechanism_narrative: A two-month consecutive decline in GDPC1 personal consumption exceeding 1% suggests weakening consumer demand, which elevates uncertainty and compresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < previous month for two consecutive months, drop ≥ 1%
failure_condition: SPX 5d forward returns are not negative (p > 0.1) during confirmed late-cycle demand weakness.

mechanism_narrative: When INDPRO and RSAFS both fall by at least 2% in the same month, indicating simultaneous supply-side shocks, the S&P 500 anticipates higher uncertainty and produces negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month AND RSAFS < previous month, with each decline ≥ 2%
failure_condition: SPX 20d forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during such double contraction months.
